question:
A 58-year-old male with no prior health issues presents with a two-day history of diarrhea, nausea, and
abdominal cramping following a week-long family vacation in Mexico. He experiences five to six daily
bowel movements that provide relief from cramping, along with chills and sweats. While able to
consume simple foods, he expresses concern about work absence due to ongoing symptoms. His
family members who traveled with him remain asymptomatic. Physical examination reveals stable
hemodynamics and a temperature of 39.4°C. His abdomen shows normal bowel sounds and mild,
diffuse tenderness on palpation, without distention, rebound, or guarding. Rectal examination reveals
blood in the stool. After collecting a stool sample for culture and initiating oral rehydration, what is the
most appropriate next step in management while awaiting culture results? Answer Choices: (A)
Prescribe azithromycin (B) Prescribe metronidazole (C) Do not initiate antimicrobial therapy, but send a
stool sample for evaluation for ova and parasites (D) Administer loperamide for symptomatic relief (E)
Initiate intravenous fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics (F) Initiate empiric therapy with vancomycin
(G) Prescribe ciprofloxacin (H) Perform colonoscopy to evaluate for inflammatory bowel disease (I)
Recommend a bland diet and observe without antibiotics (J) Prescribe trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
 A. Recommend a bland diet and observe without antibiotics
B. Do not initiate antimicrobial therapy, but send a stool sample for evaluation for ova and parasites
C. Perform colonoscopy to evaluate for inflammatory bowel disease
D. Initiate empiric therapy with vancomycin
E. Administer loperamide for symptomatic relief
F. Prescribe metronidazole
G. Prescribe azithromycin
H. Prescribe ciprofloxacin
I. Prescribe trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
J. Initiate intravenous fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics
